keys.statement: Pressure-swing distillation needs an azeotrope whose composition moves with pressure and adds no solvent. It uses more energy than extractive distillation unless the high- and low-pressure columns are heat integrated.

plain.title: Pressure-swing distillation: only for an azeotrope that moves with pressure, and heat-integrate the two columns
plain.when: You want to break an azeotrope without adding a third component.
plain.do: Check that the azeotrope composition moves with pressure. Then use two columns at different pressures, heat integrated.
plain.why: Changing the pressure moves the azeotrope, so each column can pass it. Without heat integration it uses more energy than extractive distillation.
plain.check: In CHEPTA, compute the azeotrope at both pressures and confirm that it moves enough.

decisions.obstacle: Breaking an azeotrope without a third component.
decisions.mechanism: Changing pressure moves the azeotrope composition.
decisions.operation: Two columns at different pressures, heat integrated.

keys.statement: For tetrahydrofuran + water, pressure-swing distillation showed better controllability than extractive distillation, whose added solvent and longer time constants complicate control.

plain.title: Tetrahydrofuran and water: pressure-swing distillation was easier to control than extractive distillation
plain.when: You choose between pressure-swing and extractive distillation for tetrahydrofuran and water.
plain.why: The added solvent of extractive distillation brings more interactions and longer time constants, which complicate control.
plain.check: Compare both routes' responses to feed disturbances in a dynamic model; a steady-state simulation alone cannot show controllability.

decisions.mechanism: A third component adds interactions and slower dynamics.
decisions.expected_change: A route that can be operated.

keys.statement: A cited steady-state comparison for tetrahydrofuran + water found extractive distillation cheaper per year than pressure-swing distillation; the authors argue controllability should be weighed from the start as well.

plain.title: Tetrahydrofuran and water: extractive distillation was cheaper at steady state, but weigh control too
plain.when: You compare extractive and pressure-swing distillation for tetrahydrofuran and water on cost.
plain.do: Compare on annual cost and on controllability; expect a trade-off, not a single winner, as Mtogo et al. 2021 argue.
plain.why: Extractive distillation used less energy at steady state in a study cited by Mtogo et al. 2021, not read by Lab.
plain.check: Recompute both annual costs on the same basis.

decisions.mechanism: Lower energy for the extractive route.
decisions.operation: Compare on annual cost and on controllability.
decisions.expected_change: A trade-off, not a single winner.
